answer: The tender times each pearl dive and reads the depth gauge, signing the log for every diver who goes down. A cipher dive claimed from the boat fails the log: at the quartz of the gauge the depth must match the diver's own descent, and a claimed dive shows no gauge reading at all. Forging a diving season means hiring a tender, faking eighty dives and paying 12,800, while the ivory entry in the depth log is checked at every sale of pearls, so a diver whose dives were never logged is refused a licence.
